brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 74% over 30s (28/108 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $4,770/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

brief.recommendation: Memory MEM-4 records a verified ineffective termination of batch_replayable_price_sync (checkout dropped to 29% success). The Auditor lessons require coordinated scheduler pause + termination + verification, which we cannot execute. Waiting costs ~$47,386 (BIZ-7) and EXCEEDS the 60s degradation tolerance. The workload is BATCH_REPLAYABLE with may_interrupt policy (BIZ-5), but termination alone is vetoed by memory. Escalation to the pricing team (owner per BIZ-5) is the only path that respects the verified failure and the coordination requirement.

audit.report: A batch job (batch_replayable_price_sync, pid 14427) held an idle-in-transaction lock for 4 seconds, blocking one session and contributing to checkout timeouts. Checkout success dropped to 86% (4 of 28 requests failed over 10s) against a 95% SLO, putting $2,629/min of revenue at risk with only 60s of tolerated degradation. The Database Guardian proposed terminating the blocker, but a prior memory (MEM-4) recorded that termination alone previously failed verification (checkout fell to 29%). The Continuity Guardian accepted escalation because the required coordinated pause-and-terminate procedure could not be executed automatically. The incident was escalated to the pricing team after one round lasting 18.6s; no automated action was taken.
audit.root_cause: An idle-in-transaction batch_replayable_price_sync job held a lock that blocked checkout sessions, and the only known remediation (termination) was vetoed by a prior failed verification.
lessons: For batch_replayable_price_sync: add a pre-check that the scheduler is paused before any termination attempt, because MEM-4 proves termination without scheduler coordination fails verification.
For batch_replayable_price_sync: implement a lock timeout or statement timeout on the job so it cannot hold locks idle-in-transaction longer than the 60s business tolerance window.

For batch_replayable_price_sync: create a verified runbook that atomically pauses the scheduler, terminates the job, and runs the business verification, so the guardians can execute it without human escalation.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians correctly honored the MEM-4 veto and the business-calculator trade-off; neither wasted a round, but the negotiation could not proceed to action because the required coordinated procedure was not encoded as an executable candidate.
follow_ups: Pricing team to confirm whether the scheduler for price_sync can be paused via API and document the exact pause-terminate-verify sequence.
Engineering to add a lock_timeout/statement_timeout to the batch_replayable_price_sync job definition.
Platform team to codify the coordinated pause-terminate-verify workflow as a new candidate action for future negotiations.
